sources.why: Review-aggregation roundup, no own testing, but names 240W+40Gbps cables
sources.evidence: The Anker 765 USB-C Cable (6ft, $15) is the best all-around USB-C cable — USB-IF certified 240W charging, 40Gbps data transfer, and 8K video support in one cable.
At $12, this undercuts Anker while delivering the same USB4 Gen 3 spec. Cable Matters is less known but highly respected on r/UsbCHardware.

sources.evidence: Do not assume a 240W cable is a fast data cable. The UGREEN 6.6-foot cable demonstrates the distinction: it supports 240W charging but only 480Mbps data and no video.

sources.why: Tested general guide; visible pick is a charging-only cable
sources.evidence: You should also know that the lack of faster data transfers also means the Anker cable can’t be used to hook your laptop up to a USB-C port for video.

sources.evidence: Still delivers the full 240W charging profile, so it does not force a tradeoff between data and power

missing: Proof that the cables actually deliver 240W and 40Gbps at the same time, for example a measured SSD transfer while a laptop draws over 200W, plus current prices across the USB-IF certified USB4 240W cables (Anker, Cable Matters, Amazon Basics, j5create, ACT, StarTech) and a note on which ones are really Thunderbolt 4 compatible.
why: Macworld, a major reviewer that claims hands-on testing, names specific cables that do 240W and 40Gbps (Anker 515 USB4, OWC). PCWorld also tests, but what's visible here only shows a charging-only pick. The rest are review-aggregation roundups, single product pages and retailer listings. A focused page could get in, but it would be up against Macworld's tested guide.
